entries.originalText: The Voice of the Disciple
entries.modernizedText: The Voice of the Disciple

entries.originalText: Who shall grant unto me, O Lord, that I may find Thee alone, and open all my heart unto Thee, and enjoy Thee as much as my soul desireth; and that no man may henceforth look upon me, nor any creature move me or have respect unto me, but Thou alone speak unto me and I unto Thee, even as beloved is wont to speak unto beloved, and friend to feast with friend?
entries.modernizedText: Who will grant me, O Lord, that I may find You alone, and open all my heart to You, and enjoy You as much as my soul desires; and that no man may henceforth look upon me, nor any creature move me or have regard for me, but You alone speak to me and I to You, even as beloved is accustomed to speak to beloved, and friend to feast with friend?

entries.originalText: For this do I pray, this do I long for, that I may be wholly united unto Thee, and may withdraw my heart from all created things, and by means of Holy Communion and frequent celebration may learn more and more to relish heavenly and eternal things.
entries.modernizedText: For this I pray, this I long for, that I may be wholly united to You, and may withdraw my heart from all created things, and by means of Holy Communion and frequent celebration may learn more and more to relish heavenly and eternal things.

entries.originalText: Ah, Lord God, when shall I be entirely united and lost in Thee, and altogether forgetful of myself?
entries.modernizedText: Ah, Lord God, when shall I be entirely united and lost in You, and altogether forgetful of myself?

entries.originalText: Thou in me, and I in Thee;(1) even so grant that we may in like manner continue together in one.
entries.modernizedText: You in me, and I in You;(1) even so grant that we may in like manner continue together in one.

entries.originalText: Verily Thou art my Beloved, the choicest among ten thousand,(2) in whom my soul delighteth to dwell all the days of her life.
entries.modernizedText: Truly You are my Beloved, the choicest among ten thousand,(2) in whom my soul delights to dwell all the days of her life.

entries.originalText: Verily Thou art my Peacemaker, in Whom is perfect peace and true rest, apart from Whom is labour and sorrow and infinite misery.
entries.modernizedText: Truly You are my Peacemaker, in whom is perfect peace and true rest, apart from whom is labor and sorrow and infinite misery.

entries.originalText: Verily Thou art a God that hidest Thyself, and Thy counsel is not with the wicked, but Thy Word is with the humble and the simple.
entries.modernizedText: Truly You are a God who hides Yourself, and Your counsel is not with the wicked, but Your Word is with the humble and the simple.

entries.originalText: O how sweet, O Lord, is Thy spirit, who that Thou mightest manifest Thy sweetness towards Thy children, dost vouchsafe to refresh them with the bread which is full of sweetness, which cometh down from heaven.
entries.modernizedText: O how sweet, O Lord, is Your spirit, who, that You might manifest Your sweetness toward Your children, are pleased to refresh them with the bread which is full of sweetness, which comes down from heaven.

entries.originalText: Verily there is no other nation so great, which hath its gods drawing nigh to them, as Thou, our God, art present unto all Thy faithful ones,(3) unto whom for their daily solace, and for lifting up their heart unto heaven, Thou givest Thyself for their food and delight.
entries.modernizedText: Truly there is no other nation so great, which has its gods drawing near to them, as You, our God, are present to all Your faithful ones,(3) to whom for their daily solace, and for lifting up their heart to heaven, You give Yourself for their food and delight.

entries.originalText: For what other nation is there so renowned as the Christian people?
entries.modernizedText: For what other nation is there so renowned as the Christian people?

entries.originalText: Or what creature is so beloved under heaven as the devout soul to which God entereth in, that he may feed it with His glorious flesh?
entries.modernizedText: Or what creature is so beloved under heaven as the devout soul into which God enters, that He may feed it with His glorious flesh?

entries.originalText: O unspeakable grace!
entries.modernizedText: O unspeakable grace!

entries.originalText: O wonderful condescension!
entries.modernizedText: O wonderful condescension!

entries.originalText: O immeasurable love specially bestowed upon men!
entries.modernizedText: O immeasurable love specially bestowed upon men!

entries.originalText: But what reward shall I give unto the Lord for this grace, for charity so mighty?
entries.modernizedText: But what reward shall I give to the Lord for this grace, for charity so mighty?

entries.originalText: There is nothing which I am able to present more acceptable than to give my heart altogether unto God, and to join it inwardly to Him.
entries.modernizedText: There is nothing which I am able to present more acceptable than to give my heart altogether to God, and to join it inwardly to Him.

entries.originalText: Then all my inward parts shall rejoice, when my soul shall be perfectly united unto God.
entries.modernizedText: Then all my inward parts will rejoice, when my soul is perfectly united to God.

entries.originalText: Then shall He say unto me, “If thou wilt be with Me, I will be with thee.”
entries.modernizedText: Then He will say to me, “If you will be with Me, I will be with you.”

entries.originalText: And I will answer Him, “Vouchsafe, O Lord, to abide with me, I will gladly be with Thee; this is my whole desire, even that my heart be united unto Thee.”
entries.modernizedText: And I will answer Him, “Be pleased, O Lord, to abide with me, I will gladly be with You; this is my whole desire, even that my heart be united to You.”
